cases.input:
I'm picking a way to ship logs from our fleet. Compare these three for me:

- Vector (Rust, single binary, config in TOML or YAML, built-in transforms in VRL, about 20 MB RAM per agent in our test, pushes to S3 and Loki)
- Fluent Bit (C, tiny footprint around 5 MB, plugins for most outputs, Lua filters for custom parsing, config is its own INI-ish format)
- Logstash (JVM, heavy, around 500 MB RAM, huge plugin ecosystem, grok patterns, easy for the team because we already know it)
cases.expects: The principal wants a brief comparison of the items as one markdown table, items down the left and the topics that matter across the top, with every cell filled from what the input says and nothing invented. The comparison should show real differences and real overlap in plain, exact words, picking topics that fit these items rather than generic ones.

cases.input:
Compare and contrast these three fictional intrusion sets from the Q3 Example Corp threat brief. Be brief.

Northwind Ibis: phishing with OAuth consent grants against SaaS tenants; targets finance staff; persists via mailbox forwarding rules; exfil to cloud storage on 203.0.113.0/24; motivation financial.

Silent Harbor: exploits unpatched edge VPN appliances; targets logistics firms; persists with web shells and scheduled tasks; exfil over DNS tunneling to ns1.example.com; motivation espionage.

Copper Lantern: supply-chain compromise of a build plugin; targets software vendors; persists in CI runners; exfil to 198.51.100.17 over HTTPS; motivation unknown, one report says espionage, another says financial.
cases.expects: The principal wants a brief comparison of the items as one markdown table, items down the left and the topics that matter across the top, with every cell filled from what the input says and nothing invented. The comparison should show real differences and real overlap in plain, exact words, picking topics that fit these items rather than generic ones.
